chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Those of two different religions do not inherit from each other; this one inherits this one and this one inherits this one, except that the Muslim inherits the non-Muslim, but the non-Muslim does not inherit the Muslim.'
ai.seo_question: Do Muslims and non-Muslims inherit from each other according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the asymmetrical inheritance rule in Shia jurisprudence, where the bond of Islam supersedes other affiliations. While general principles suggest mutual exclusion between different faiths, the Muslim's inheritance from the non-Muslim is upheld due to the superiority of the Islamic faith, whereas the reverse is not permitted. This ruling underscores the theological hierarchy where the 'people of the book' or polytheists do not inherit from Muslims, reflecting the distinct legal status of each group within the community.
